defects.label: fix
defects.summary: Lifecycle dependency mismatch: render runs before finalize, but finalize writes search assets that rendered pages must reference. This becomes brittle/incorrect if search artifacts use sharded/chunked or content-hash filenames. The plan must define a manifest/contract or reorder phases so renderer can reference the correct search asset paths deterministically.

evidence.quote: Standardize lifecycle hooks consistent with O2: init → collectFiles → transform → resolve → render → finalize
Hook: render(context) → HTML files and static theme assets written to output directory using context data.
Hook: finalize(context) → search index artifacts written to output directory (optionally sharded).
can evolve to sharding/chunking if needed.

evidence.note: Narrative expects rendered pages to reference search artifacts produced by finalize.

patch.value: Standardize lifecycle hooks consistent with O2: init → collectFiles → transform → resolve → finalize → render; run hooks deterministically with explicit ordering rules. (If keeping render before finalize, the search plugin MUST predeclare stable asset paths/manifest before render so HTML can reference deterministic URLs.)

CLI invokes the Core Orchestrator (C8), which loads config, registers plugins, and executes a deterministic lifecycle: init → collectFiles → transform → resolve → finalize → render. (1) File Collector plugin (C9) scans the input root and populates context.noteRegistry with file paths and stable slugs. (2) Markdown Parser plugin (C10) parses each note, extracts frontmatter, and normalizes internal links into a canonical representation attached to each note. (3) Resolver plugins run in resolve: Backlink Resolver (C11) builds the corpus link graph and attaches backlinks; Tag Aggregator (C12) builds tag indices and registers tag pages. (4) Search Index plugin (C13) builds and writes client-side index artifacts to the output AND exposes a deterministic manifest/asset root in context. (5) Renderer/Theme plugin (C14) generates HTML pages and static assets from the enriched context (including backlinks/tags) and references the search manifest/asset root; the Client-Side Runtime (C15) provides in-browser search UX. All outputs are static files only, suitable for static hosting.
